rationale: TYPE-PARAMETER BOUNDS (owner ruling 2026-10-18, Java-only constructs item: 'type-parameter bounds'). JLS 4.4: a bound names a type, so `class Bounds<T extends Number & Comparable<T>>` MENTIONS Number and Comparable. The lane emitted NOTHING for bounds before this site: probe pre-fix produced 2 references for the whole file (the import mention only) and zero for Number/Comparable/Serializable/Exception/CharSequence. `script/m14/spec/java-completeness.json` G6 had ruled bounds a declared LIMITATION ('bounds are rarely load-bearing'); the owner's complete-surface ruling makes that ruling obsolete, and the emission uses the label the ten already have - a bound is a type mention, so `references` with metadata.relationshipType 'type_parameter_bound', NOT a new relationship kind. `boundFor` records WHICH type parameter is constrained, because three parameters would otherwise look like three unrelated references. Authored from Java semantics before the fix; covers a class bounded by an INTERFACE with a self-referential generic argument, a second class-level parameter, a METHOD-level parameter (JLS 4.4 applies to methods the same way), a record's parameters, and an interface (JLS 9.4's type parameter) with a fully-qualified bound. One edge per bound TYPE (a bound is a type list); the `T` inside Comparable<T> is published too because the declared-type walk already publishes generic arguments - one consistency rule, not two.

forbidRelationships.comment: `extends` is a keyword inside a bound, not a type; the error-recovery shape this forbids
a bound LIST is one edge per type, never the clause text
the file wrote java.io.IOException, so the target keeps the written path (the truncation rule the throws fixture also pins)
